content.title: THIS COMMON SNACK BEATS A BANANA AT ITS OWN GAME
facts: **Dried apricots** pack nearly triple the potassium of a banana, gram for gram — a handful can outdo the fruit famous for it.
**Pumpkin seeds** carry more magnesium per ounce than a serving of spinach, and you don't need to cook them down to get it.
**Brazil nuts** are so loaded with selenium that just 2 nuts a day covers your full daily need.
**Sun-dried tomatoes** hold far more vitamin K than fresh tomatoes, since drying concentrates it.
**Pomegranate seeds** give you more fiber per cup than an apple, seeds and all.
**Kale** has more calcium per calorie than a glass of milk, which surprises most people who only chase dairy for it.
**Lentils** deliver more iron per cup than a beef steak of the same size, minus the saturated fat.
**Hemp seeds** contain more zinc per ounce than most cuts of chicken.
**Chia seeds** are one of the richest plant sources of omega-3 ALA around, 2 tbsp/day is enough to make a real dent.
**Mushrooms left in sunlight** for 10 minutes can develop meaningful vitamin D, unlike almost any other produce.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
A few of these are worth slowing down on. Brazil nuts are one of the only foods where you can genuinely overdo a mineral — selenium builds up in your system, so 2 a day is the sweet spot, not a handful. Lentils punch above their weight on iron because pairing them with something high in vitamin C, like tomatoes or citrus, helps your body actually absorb the plant-based form, which is normally harder to use than the iron in meat. And chia seeds only release their omega-3s well once they've soaked or been ground — tossing whole dry seeds on top of food means you miss out on a chunk of the benefit. Everyone's body is different, so treat these as starting points, not rules.
